chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: The Capital Lounge, Muggsy Spanier, and downtown Chicago's clubs
summary: They play State Street opposite Muggsy Spanier while Roy Eldridge, Art Van Damme, Boyd Raeburn, Cab Calloway and Duke Ellington play nearby.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: We left there and we went to Chicago to play a place called the Capital Lounge down on State Street. That was like just a paradise for a musician to be in, because at that particular time it seemed like everybody was in Chicago... There were names all over the place. We were at the Capital Lounge along with Muggsy Spanier's group, and the first time I'd ever... I'd heard about Muggsy Spanier, but I'd never met him. He was a very fine old man. He used to talk to us a lot, and he loved to come down in the dressing room with his horn and play little things, and say 'How do you like this?' - - and he'd play some pretty little things. And he played beautiful horn, you know. He had this little group that played opposite us.
Then round the corner, Roy Eldridge had a band at a place called the Preview. He had his brother, Joe, and a drummer

whose name I can't remember... Everybody used to call him Dr. Fu(?). I can't remember his name. But he and, as I said, Joe Eldridge. There was a fellow named Roswell Gayle(?), who is in California now, who is a pianist, and he's turned actor -- as a matter of fact, he's had some acting parts in pictures now, I understand; a very good friend. There was a guy who was playing bass, and he was a former saxophone player. I can't remember his name either. He smoked a cigar a lot. But anyway, they were there with Roy Eldridge. And the Preview had a revolving stage where the guys played and the stage went around, and I had never seen that happen before.

I don't know... Each one of those places had at least two bands. The Preview was on Randolph Street, and we were on State Street. Right down the street from Roy Eldridge, on the right, was a guy who later became a very famous accordion player, whose name was Art Van Damme. He had one of the most popular ever accordion trios, and he used to be fantastic on the accordion. Down the street from him was the band that recorded Dizzy's...

Boyd Raeburn. Boyd Raeburn had a big band right down on the corner. In that same place, Pete Brown, a very popular alto saxophone player back then, and played... He was one of the big names on the alto saxophone during that time. He had

a group. Down the street in the Sherman Hotel was Cab Calloway's band. Duke Ellington was playing the Stephens Hotel. There was just music everywhere, with all kinds of names. And between shows, we'd just go around and meet all these people. And I got to know so many musicians who became lifetime friends, who ended up being friends.
